clue.text: Clear to detect the lies

definitions.meaning: transparent, as glass or a thin fabric is
to spot a deception for what it is, not be fooled by it

explanation.surface: Someone advises that the way to clarity is spotting the falsehoods.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one expression: the hyphenated adjective, and the two-word verb phrase meaning to see past a pretence.
explanation.definitionFit: Transparent material lets light pass, and seeing past a deception is perceiving the truth behind it: both readings of the same phrase.

clue.text: Scrambles signal, primarily reaching foreign dishes

indicators.note: primarily asks for the opening letter of the word signal

parts.note: curries are spicy dishes of Indian origin

explanation.surface: Someone frantically sends a signal while reaching for exotic plates of food.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble is to hurry in a disorderly rush, a synonym of scuttling along quickly.

clue.text: Rabbits run out of veg

indicators.note: out of says the run abbreviation leaves the vegetable word

parts.note: Brussels sprouts are a vegetable
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A tale of rabbits who have run out of vegetables to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbits' looks like the animals but is a verb: British slang for talking on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering at length, a synonym of holding forth tediously.

clue.text: Air final part of Love Island

parts.note: the air above is the sky

indicators.note: final part of asks for the closing letter of the word Love

explanation.surface: An item about the airing of the last episode of the reality show Love Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like a verb (to broadcast) but gives SKY; Skye is a Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is a large island off the west coast of Scotland, an example of the category named.

clue.text: NYPD case to get resolved having been shortened

indicators.note: a case being resolved suggests its parts are sorted and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A New York police case is wrapped up after being cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb usually belongs to music, but it also means cutting a sound or letter out of the middle of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Syncopation in grammar is the dropping of sounds from inside a word, so a syncopated word is a contracted one.

clue.text: Regular exercise — shaving seconds off an Olympic record?

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympic Games

indicators.note: shaving ... off says a small piece is trimmed away from the record word
completes shaving ... off, taking letters away

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

explanation.surface: Training regularly in the hope of clipping a few seconds from an Olympic record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaving ... off' removes S (seconds) from DISC to leave DIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something periodic recurs at fixed intervals, which is what regular means here.

clue.text: First couple from Scotland seen on border with English map

parts.note: the opening two letters of Scotland, which also make its usual abbreviation
a hem is the edge or border of a garment

explanation.surface: A Scottish couple turn up at the border carrying an English map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'map' is a verb here, as in map out a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To map out something is to plan it in detail, a synonym of devising a plan for it.

clue.text: Tone down adult clues for this?

definitions.meaning: a colour or shade, like that of the sky
risqué or smutty, as in an X-rated film

explanation.surface: Someone asks for adult clues to be toned down.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: the clue then tells you these three words are clues for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a colour, means melancholy, and describes indecent material such as off-colour jokes or films.

clue.text: Houdini act — legend that will clear 22 down in 10

parts.note: Harry Houdini was famous for escapes
a map's legend is its key, explaining the symbols

explanation.surface: Houdini's escape trick, a legend that clears the way from a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 down and 10 point to a spreadsheet cell in Microsoft's program; pressing the keyboard button named cancels what has been typed into it.
explanation.definitionFit: On a computer keyboard this button cancels input, abandoning an edit to a spreadsheet cell.

clue.text: Sounds like very big is better?

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the verb, to be better than others

indicators.note: Sounds like says the letters for very big are said out loud

parts.note: XL is the clothing size extra large

explanation.surface: A question whether bigger really is better.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo or surpass others is to be superior to them, which is what being better means.

clue.text: See 12
Houdini's act two recurrence — lethal ties loosened

indicators.note: ties being loosened suggests the letters are untied and freely rearranged

explanation.surface: Houdini's second act repeats, with deadly bonds slackened as he escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: The 23 letters of the phrase are all rearranged; 'loosened' is the signal, fitting the image of bonds slipped underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Houdini's famous stunt had him suspended upside down, locked in a glass water tank from which he escaped.

clue.text: Stop! Time to get out without wearing straps

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around another
to get out says the time letter leaves the word for stop

parts.note: to stop is to rest
wearing a coat is being in a coat

explanation.surface: A cry to halt, with time to escape from restraints when not dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'to get out' takes the time letter away.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins are the leather straps used to guide and control a horse.

clue.text: Spot journalist and paper giving false hope

parts.note: a pip is a spot on a die or playing card
ED is short for editor
a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A reporter spots a newspaper giving people unfounded optimism.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an unrealistic fantasy, said to come from opium smokers' visions.

clue.text: Plays around with free 20 hand

indicators.note: free means the letters are released and placed in a new order

parts.note: refers to the answer at 20 down

explanation.surface: Someone fools about with a gripping tool in one free hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who philanders conducts casual affairs, a synonym of sleeping around.

clue.text: Mrs needs no foreign currency

indicators.note: foreign suggests the letters are made strange, an altered arrangement

explanation.surface: A married woman has no use for foreign money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currency' looks like money but means being current or up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Currency can mean the quality of being current, the same as being up to date.

clue.text: Simple Harry Houdini act with steps

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so these letters are knocked out of order; Houdini's first name too

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Harry Houdini's act was simple, done in a few steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like Houdini's first name but is the signal to rearrange HOUDINI ACT plus STEPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsophisticated means naive or plain, lacking refinement, which simple covers.

clue.text: Pleasure-seekers find love in parking spaces by the roadside

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: in says the love letter goes inside the roadside spaces

parts.note: lay-bys are British roadside stopping areas
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Hedonists finding romance in roadside parking spots.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAY-BY is a British pull-off area beside a main road.
explanation.definitionFit: Playboys are wealthy men devoted to enjoyment, an example of people chasing pleasure.

clue.text: Tied: one's left in that place locked up?

definitions.text: Tied: one's left in that place locked up?

indicators.note: locked up says these letters are enclosed by the others
left means the one letter departs from the word tied

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
in that place means there

explanation.surface: Someone bound and left behind in a place where they are held captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tied' does double duty: it opens the wordplay, and the whole clue describes the answer. 'left' removes one, 'locked up' encloses the place word.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal or person tied by rope to a post is held fast, so the whole clue describes being bound.

clue.text: Irregular pressure: expression of surprise in danger

parts.note: ha is an exclamation of surprise
P is the physics symbol for pressure
a hazard is a danger

explanation.surface: Uneven pressure provokes a gasp at the risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Haphazard means lacking any order or plan, which is irregular or random.

clue.text: Stud could come out with these stories about royal? Prince goes first

definitions.text: Stud could come out with these

indicators.note: goes first puts the prince letter at the front
about says the stories go around the royal letter

parts.note: lies are false stories
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in regina or rex

explanation.surface: A royal stud could come out with tales about a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stud' is a metal fastener a gripping tool can pull, not a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: Pincer tools grip and pull small items, so a stud could be removed with them.

clue.text: See 12
Feature of magazine article with small piece making cover

indicators.note: making cover says these letters enclose another, covering it

parts.note: a tad is a small amount
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A magazine feature with a short piece slotted in on the cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A classified advertisement seeking an item or worker, found in magazines and newspapers.

clue.text: Reached top of cold water with arms at side

parts.note: C marks the cold water tap
limbed means having limbs, arms at the side of the body

explanation.surface: Houdini surfaces from the cold water tank, arms at his sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold water' gives C, as on a tap; LIMBED is an adjective meaning having limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbed means ascended, the act of getting to the summit of something.

clue.text: See 12
A long time after dropping cage

indicators.note: after says the long time follows the dropping

parts.note: dung is animal droppings
an eon is a very long time

explanation.surface: A long time passes after the cage falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' looks like a verb but is the noun, animal waste.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground prison cell, a place where captives are confined.

clue.text: Artist buried alive, partially

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An artist is buried alive, partly, perhaps in one of his own surreal scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was the Spanish surrealist painter famed for melting clocks.

clue.text: Fat conjuror ultimately saws woman in half

indicators.note: saws ... in half pictures the magician's trick of cutting a box in two, so one letter goes in the middle
completes saws ... in half, the letter splitting the woman word

parts.note: lady is a woman

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the closing letter of conjuror

explanation.surface: A plump magician finishes by sawing his assistant in half.
explanation.definitionFit: Lardy is British informal for fat, full of lard.

clue.text: They let out zebras regularly to chase on fields

indicators.note: to chase puts the zebra letters behind the others

parts.note: RE means on or about, as in a letter heading
leas are meadows

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of zebras

explanation.surface: Zebras are periodically let out to run around the fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who free or discharge things are releasers, people who let them go.
